public_rationale: BBC reporting dated July 3, 2024 supports the numerical component: Google's emissions in 2023 were 48% higher than in 2019 [e1]. Google separately attributed its 13% increase from 2022 to 2023 primarily to increased data-center energy consumption and supply-chain emissions [e2]. Neither item measures AI's share of the 2019–2023 increase or establishes a substantial worldwide emissions increase attributable to generative AI [e1, e2]. The overall causal claim therefore remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: The 48% comparison comes from reporting on Google's environmental report; the primary report PDF was not admitted.
The stated drivers of the 2022–2023 increase do not establish attribution for the full 2019–2023 period.
The evidence neither establishes nor refutes the claimed scale of AI's corporate and worldwide emissions effects.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Artificial intelligence, driven by generative AI, is already massively increasing global emissions, particularly from companies like Google, whose emissions rose 48% in the last five years thanks to AI.

statement.excerpt: Even if changing this were possible — and it'd be good for society if it was — artificial intelligence (driven by generative AI) is already massively increasing global emissions, particularly from companies like Google, which saw its emissions increase by 48% in the last five years thanks to AI.

from_speaker: emissions increase by 48% in the last five years
our_interpretation: Assess the reported 2019–2023 emissions comparison, the five annual observations underlying the report available before the post.
Read thanks to AI as asserting a substantial causal contribution, without requiring AI to be the only cause.
Read massively increasing global emissions as a substantial worldwide emissions effect, not merely higher electricity use or a large percentage change at one company.
Treat the numerical increase and its causal attribution as separate components.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence confirms Google's approximately 48% increase from 2019 to 2023 and establishes that AI materially caused it, alongside a substantial worldwide emissions increase attributable to AI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable emissions records refute the reported increase, or credible attribution evidence establishes that AI did not materially cause the asserted corporate and worldwide increases.

evidence.locator: First paragraph of the reproduced BBC article
evidence.publisher: BBC, reproduced by Business & Human Rights Resource Centre
evidence.explanation: Supports the numerical Google component. It does not measure how much of that increase AI caused.

evidence.locator: Section Our ongoing work to build a sustainable future
evidence.explanation: Google identifies broad operational and supply-chain drivers for the latest annual increase. Those categories can include AI, but this disclosure does not quantify AI's contribution to the five-year increase.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable emissions measurements and causal attribution for 2019–2023 that separate AI and generative AI from other activities at Google and worldwide.
